messages:
marie: Heads-up — two preemptible GPU nodepools in us-west1 were reclaimed ~2001234500 and cluster-autoscaler redistributed pods cross-region, we saw an egress spike and increased tail latency. Logs pasted below.

ops-bot: ALERT: nodepool-usw1-preemptible x2 terminated (preemption). pods evicted: 42. recommended action: check fallback routing.

aj: Which services got moved where? any latency-sensitive inference impacted?

marie: quick breakdown: realtime-inference shards (service=infer-lowlat) moved to cluster-eu-west1, batch-renderers landed in cluster-us-west2. The eu move added ~120-250ms p95 to a subset. Some payloads also hit cross-region egress.

sam: ouch. that egress cost is nontrivial if it persists — eu-west1->us-west1 egress adds up. also SLA alerts for p95.

irene: we should avoid cross-region fallbacks for latency-sensitive classes. proposal: prioritize regional dedicated/warmpool capacity, and set node affinity/anti-affinity fallback rules. Example pod affinity (quick):

```
nodeAffinity:
  preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
  - weight: 100
    preference:
      matchExpressions:
      - key: redwood/region
        operator: In
        values: [us-west1]
```

This keeps latency-critical pods local unless no capacity.

david: also we can tune cluster-autoscaler to prefer least-waste and balance similar nodegroups so it tries warm pools first: `--expander=least-waste` + `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` on CA. Coupled with `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` so nodes aren't torn down too fast.

claire: Another lever: taint dedicated pools with `dedicated=true:NoSchedule` and give latency-critical pods a toleration. Preemptible jobs get a different toleration so scheduler avoids moving critical jobs into preemptible pools automatically.

marie: For immediate mitigation I: 1) forced 6 inference shards back to west1-dedicated, 2) bumped warmpool size in us-west1 by +3 GPUs, 3) applied affinity snippet to infer-lowlat. Also started an egress budget - will throttle cross-region fallback if cost > threshold.

aj: For longer-term: can we add a routing policy at the inference gateway that prefers same-region endpoints and fails to local replica rather than routing across regions? That avoids scheduler shuffling entirely.

irene: yes, can add policy. We should also add a cluster-level annotation `redwood/fallback-policy: regional-only` and have the placement controller respect it. Also consider adding lease-based warmpool (keep small committed nodes).

david: small config tweak that helped us before: reduce `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 5m for preemptible pools but keep 15m for dedicated pools. Keeps a short buffer without burning cost. Also enable CA `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` in case local scratch matters.

marie: I'll open a follow-up RFC for routing + scheduler changes. For the postmortem, items: (a) CA expander defaults, (b) no regional fallback policy, (c) insufficient warm pool commit. I'll assign owners.

ops-bot: TICKET CREATED: INC-2734 - "preemptible eviction caused cross-region failover and egress spike" (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2734)

sam: Thanks team. Quick ask: can we get temporary egress credits approved while we fix route policy? @finance? :pray:

marie: pinged finance privately. also scheduling a quick postmortem sync at 15:30 PT.

aj: :thumbsup:
